deep_dive.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation for Ensemble Determinization MCTS
deep_dive.abstract: Simulation-based algorithms are especially suited for high-uncertainty environments such as adversarial board games with significant elements of randomness and hidden information. In particular, several Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) variants are commonly used in such domains. In this paper, we propose a series of enhancements for Ensemble Determinization MCTS, introducing two axes for dynamic resource allocation. First, Dynamic Number of Determinizations, increases or decreases the number of currently used determinization trees depending on the behavior of so-far search. Second, Dynamic Simulation Allocation, splits the simulation budget nonuniformly across the determinization trees, using simulation-to-simulation decisions to choose the tree with potentially the best knowledge gain. As benchmark domains, we used three popular tabletop games: Jaipur, Lost Cities, and Splendor. Testing our proposed enhancements in iteration- and time-based settings showed that particular configurations yield a statistically significant increase in the algorithm's strength.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Proposes dynamic resource allocation for Ensemble Determinization MCTS, improving search efficiency in adversarial board games with randomness and hidden information, directly relevant as an extension of MCTS used in AlphaZero.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 该论文针对具有随机性和隐藏信息的对抗性棋盘游戏，提出了一种面向集成确定化MCTS的动态资源分配增强方法。通过动态调整确定化树的数量和非均匀分配模拟预算，显著提升了搜索效率。由于MCTS是AlphaZero的核心组件，该工作可视为AlphaZero架构的一种扩展或改进，为提升AlphaZero类算法在复杂博弈环境中的性能提供了新思路。
